'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[TDF–OLA joint offensive]]
***The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Greece)|Greek foreign minstry]] urges Greek citizens to evacuate from [[Ethiopia]]. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/news/1172717/foreign-ministry-urges-greek-nationals-to-leave-ethiopia/ (''Rkathimerini'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] [[Foreign Secretary (United Kingdom)|foreign secretary]] [[Liz Truss]] warns [[Russia]] that any attack on [[Ukraine]] would be a "grave mistake", and that the UK is working closely with its [[NATO]] allies to provide support to Ukraine. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/exclusive-britain-says-russian-attack-ukraine-would-be-grave-mistake-2021-11-24/ (Reuters)]
**Ukraine launches a "special operation" on the [[Belarus–Ukraine border|Belarusian border]] involving troops from the [[National Guard of Ukraine|National Guard]], [[National Police of Ukraine|police]], and the [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|armed forces]], including anti-tank and airborne units, amid fears of a [[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis|migrant crisis]] and also due to a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian military]] build-up on [[State Border of Ukraine|its border]]s. [https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-border-operation-belarus/31576562.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Anglophone Crisis]]
**Gunmen open fire at a school in [[Ekondo-Titi]], [[Southwest Region (Cameroon)|Southwest Region]], [[Cameroon]], killing three children and a teacher. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/four-killed-in-school-in-troubled-anglophone-cameroon-01637770808 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israel]] carries out [[airstrike]]s in [[Homs]], [[Syria]], killing two civilians and injuring six [[Syrian Armed Forces|soldiers]] and another civilian. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/11/24/syria-says-israeli-airstrike-in-homs-leaves-2-dead-7-wounded (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[English Channel migrant crossings (2018–present)|English Channel migrant crossings]]
**[[November 2021 English Channel disaster]]
***Twenty-seven people drown after a [[dinghy]] carrying migrants sinks in the [[English Channel]] near [[Calais]], [[France]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-59406355 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The Andorran government decrees to extend the access control with the immunity passport to restaurants, gyms, museums, hotels and hairdressers for those over 16 years of age. [https://www.andorradifusio.ad/noticies/passaport-covid-sera-obligatori-restauracio-partir-divendres (''Andorra Difusió'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Czech Republic]] reports a record 25,864 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/coronavirus-infections-hit-new-record-high-in-czech-republic/2021/11/24/fae35936-4d10-11ec-a7b8-9ed28bf23929_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] reports a record 12,637 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.045 million. [https://news.trust.org/item/20211124075957-ni63v/ (Thomson Reuters Foundation)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The [[Italy|Italian]] [[Government of Italy|government]] signs a decree that will ban people who are not [[COVID-19 vaccination in Italy|vaccinated]] or who have not recovered from COVID-19 from entering indoor venues (not including workplaces) from December 6 until January 15 and will also extend the vaccine mandate to teachers, [[Italian police|police]], and the [[Italian military|military]] beginning on December 15. It also imposes the use of the "green pass" to all types of public transport, including for people with negative COVID-19 tests. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/italy-restrict-access-unvaccinated-indoor-venues-sources-2021-11-24/ (Reuters)] [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/cronaca/2021/11/24/arriva-il-super-green-pass-a-tempo-ecco-cosa-cambia_d1dab997-ee78-4367-889d-40a3a8a97746.html (ANSA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] reimposes mandatory {{cvt|1.5|m}} [[social distancing]] measures in places where COVID passports are not required, amid an increase in the number of new COVID-19 cases. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/11/23/social-distancing-mandatory-as-dutch-covid-infections-spike (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia]]
****The [[Slovakia|Slovak]] [[Government of Slovakia|government]] declares a 90-day [[state of emergency]] and will impose a two-week [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for the entire country beginning tomorrow, which will close all non-essential shops and restaurants and limit a person's movement to specific reasons only as the country reports a record 10,315 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.politico.eu/article/coronavirus-out-of-control-slovakia-two-week-lockdown/ (''Politico.eu'')]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control]] recommends that the [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] should be given to all adults aged above 18 years six months after received their second dose, with priority given to those aged above 40 years. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/europe-health-agency-in-shift-urges-faster-covid-19-booster-rollout-as-cases-surge-11637776090 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****It is announced that [[Merck & Co.]]'s antiviral drug [[molnupiravir]] will be available to [[Filipinos|Philippine]] patients after the [[Food and Drug Administration (Philippines)|Food and Drug Administration]] issued a compassionate special permit for the drug and an agreement was signed between the [[Office of the Vice President of the Philippines]] and a local health care provider. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1518590/molnupiravir-available-to-ovps-telemedicine-patients-who-are-prescribed-to-take-it (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[Travel during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Singapore]] and [[Malaysia]] agree to the opening of a second quarantine-free vaccinated travel lane through the [[Johor–Singapore Causeway]] beginning on November 29 using designated bus lanes, which will mark the reopening of the land border between the two countries. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/malaysia-land-vtl-nov-29-travellers-designated-bus-services-2335266 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports a record 4,116 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 425,065. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/south-korea-new-cases-serious-cases-hospitalisation-elderly-patients-2334716 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Canada]]
***[[Health Canada]] grants full approval for the [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine]], making [[Canada]] the first country to fully approve the single-dose vaccine. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/public-global-health/582997-canada-becomes-first-nation-to-give-full-approval-to (''The Hill'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Ethiopia–Ireland relations]]
**The [[Department of Foreign Affairs (Ireland)|Irish Department of Foreign Affairs]] advises all [[Irish citizen]]s to leave Ethiopia immediately, due to the [[Tigray War|ongoing conflict]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2021/1124/1262889-irish-embassy-ethiopia/ (RTÉ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2015–present Polish constitutional crisis]]
**[[2015 Polish Constitutional Court crisis]]
***In response to the ruling of the [[European Court of Human Rights]] in ''Xero Flor w Polsce sp. z o.o. v. Poland'', which found that the business was denied the [[right to fair trial]] because a judge of the Tribunal was appointed illegally, the [[Constitutional Tribunal (Poland)|Constitutional Tribunal]] declares that it is not a court within the meaning of [[Article 6 of the European Convention on Human Rights|Article 6]] of the [[European Convention on Human Rights]] and rules that the ECHR did not have the right to control the validity of appointments of the Tribunal's judges. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polish-tribunal-rules-european-rights-court-cannot-question-its-judges-2021-11-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Murder of Ahmaud Arbery]]
**The three men who killed Ahmaud Arbery in [[Brunswick, Georgia]], [[United States]], in February 2020 are [[Guilt (law)|found guilty]] of [[murder (United States law)|murder]] and [[aggravated assault]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-us-canada-59379518 (BBC News)]
*[[2021 Solomon Islands unrest]]
**Protesters take to the streets in [[Honiara]], [[Solomon Islands]], calling for the [[resignation]] of incumbent [[Prime Minister of Solomon Islands|prime minister]] [[Manasseh Sogavare]]. A building within the [[National Parliament of Solomon Islands|Parliament complex]] is set on fire as protesters engage in [[looting]] and [[arson]] while [[Royal Solomon Islands Police Force|law enforcement personnel]] fire [[tear gas]] into crowds. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/456476/buildings-burned-in-looting-after-solomon-islands-protest (RNZ)] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/456444/protesters-take-to-the-streets-in-solomon-islands (RNZ)]
*Two allies of [[Russian opposition]] leader and activist [[Alexei Navalny]] leave Russia, becoming the latest people to do so after many of Navalny's allies left the country in September. The two people are identified as a woman who helped Navalny represent his organization and a lawyer who said that he was under pressure. [https://www.reuters.com/world/two-navalny-allies-flee-russia-he-challenges-extremist-tag-2021-11-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Government of Australia|Australia]] designates the [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] [[Shia Islam|Shia]] [[militant]] group [[Hezbollah]] and the [[Neo-Nazism|neo-Nazi]] [[paramilitary]] group [[The Base (hate group)|The Base]] as [[terrorist organisation]]s. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/nov/24/australia-lists-neo-nazi-group-the-base-and-hezbollah-as-terrorist-organisations (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*Aftermath of the [[2021 German federal election]]
**The [[Social Democratic Party of Germany]], the [[Free Democratic Party of Germany]], and [[Alliance 90/The Greens]] agree to a "[[traffic light coalition]]" to form the next government with [[Olaf Scholz]] of the SPD as the next [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]], succeeding [[Angela Merkel]]. The government will be formally elected by the [[Bundestag]] in early December. [https://www.politico.eu/article/future-german-government-to-present-coalition-deal-this-afternoon/ (''Politico'')]
*[[Sweden]]'s [[Riksdag]] votes for [[Social Democratic Party of Sweden|Social Democrat]] leader [[Magdalena Andersson]] to become the first female [[prime minister of Sweden]]. However, Andersson resigned several hours later, after the [[Green Party (Sweden)|Green Party]] quit the coalition. The Greens quit the coalition after the opposition budget was approved by the Riksdag. [https://sverigesradio.se/artikel/andersson-clears-vote-to-become-swedens-first-female-prime-minister (Radio Sweden)] [https://www.reuters.com/markets/rates-bonds/swedish-pm-resigns-first-day-after-coalition-collapses-2021-11-24/ (Reuters)]
